title: Host — n5pro (Minisforum N5 Pro, HX 370)
description: Everything observable on the n5pro chassis: power, thermals, CPU, memory, network and storage. This board has the richer sensor surface of the two — eight temperature chips including DDR5 module sensors and NIC PHY temperatures — and, unlike eq12, NO readable fan tachometer at all. The spinning disks are passed through to the TrueNAS VM and are not visible here; see the NAS dashboard for those.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since last boot (`system_uptime`).

panels.title: Load (1m)
panels.description: 1-minute run-queue length. This host has 24 logical CPUs, so sustained load above that means work is queueing rather than running.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: 100 minus idle, across all cores.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Of 96 GiB total.

panels.title: Package power
panels.description: CPU package power from the RAPL energy counter. THIS IS NOT WALL POWER — it excludes the drives, the fans and PSU conversion loss, and this machine has no wall meter.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description: Maximum across every temperature reading on the board, whatever chip it came from. Use the Thermals row to see which one it is.

panels.title: Chassis fan
panels.description: There is no fan telemetry on this machine. The ITE IT5571 controller is vendor-gated and its EC publishes zeros, and no ACPI cooling-device objects are exposed either. This tile is expected to be empty — see the Cooling row.

panels.title: Root filesystem
panels.description: Usage of `/`.

panels.title: CPU power by RAPL domain
panels.description: Only `package-0` is exported on this board. It also exposes a domain NAMED `core`, and that domain is EXCLUDED deliberately: a load-placement test showed it stayed flat at 0.12 W while package climbed 28 W under a three-core load that avoided CPU0, so it covers CPU0 alone and is not the all-core aggregate its name implies. eq12's identically-named domain IS a genuine aggregate. Coverage is a property of the board, never of the name (#194).

panels.title: iGPU power and clock
panels.description: The Radeon 890M's package power tracker (`ppt`) and shader clock. Two different units, so two axes would be wrong — the clock is drawn on its own panel below rather than overlaid here.

panels.title: iGPU shader clock
panels.description: `sclk` from the amdgpu driver. Idles at 600 MHz on this part.

panels.title: Every temperature sensor
panels.description: One series per chip/feature pair reported by lm-sensors. The chip tag is what disambiguates identically-named features across different chips.

panels.title: NVMe (SMART)
panels.description: Drive-reported composite temperature from smartctl, which is a different sensor path from the `nvme-pci-*` hwmon chip above — they should track, and a divergence is interesting.

panels.title: No fan telemetry on this board — a measured negative

options.content:
This machine exposes **no readable fan speed**, and that is a finding rather than a gap in this dashboard.

- The Super-I/O is an **ITE IT5571**, which no in-tree hwmon driver binds. Unlike eq12's IT8613E, there is no `force_id` that reaches it.
- Direct **EC RAM dumps read zeros** — the controller is vendor-gated, so the data is not merely unexposed, it is not published to the host at all.
- **No ACPI cooling-device objects** either, so there is not even the state-only signal eq12 has.

Cooling is therefore inferred from **temperature trend**, not measured directly. The thermals row above is the fan panel for this host: if the cooling fails, temperature is where it shows.

Full detail and the commands that established it: `docs/n5pro.md`.

panels.title: Thermal headroom
panels.description: Distance from each sensor to its own critical threshold, where the chip publishes one. This is the closest thing to a cooling-health signal available on this board: with no tachometer, a fan failure appears here as headroom collapsing across several chips at once.

panels.title: CPU time by mode
panels.description: Stacked to 100%. `iowait` climbing means the CPU is waiting on storage, not busy; `steal` is only meaningful under virtualisation.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 1 / 5 / 15 minute run-queue length. The dashed reference is 24 logical CPUs.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: `used` excludes cache and buffers. On a ZFS host a large slab/ARC is normal and is not a leak.

panels.title: Swap and processes
panels.description: Swap in/out rate is the signal that matters — a large swap *used* with zero rate is just cold pages.

panels.title: Physical NIC throughput
panels.description: `nic0` and `nic1` are the physical ports; `vmbr0`/`vmbr1` bridge them and `vmbr2` is the host-only bridge carrying NFS to the TrueNAS VM over 10.99.99.x. NIC PHY and MAC temperatures for `nic1` are in the Thermals row above — this board reports those, which is unusual.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Both should be flat at zero. A non-zero rate here is a cable, a duplex mismatch, or a saturated ring buffer — it will show up as latency long before it shows up as an outage.

panels.title: Guest interface throughput
panels.description: Per-guest taps and veths, which is how you attribute host network load to a particular VM or container.

panels.title: Link speed
panels.description: Negotiated link speed in Mb/s per physical interface and bridge.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Whole devices only — partitions are excluded so the same bytes are not counted twice.

panels.title: Disk utilisation and latency
panels.description: `io_util` is the fraction of wall time the device had a request in flight. Sustained 100% means the device is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Filesystem usage
panels.description: ZFS datasets and the root filesystem.

panels.title: NVMe health (SMART)
panels.description: `health_ok` is smartctl's overall verdict: 1 is passing. `percentage_used` is the drive's own wear estimate — it can exceed 100 and is not a capacity figure. `available_spare` falling toward its threshold is the number that predicts failure.
